items.title: 'It is just as wrong to make social media the sole cause of adolescent distress as it is to deny its power to amplify it'
items.description: Our responsibility as adults is neither to abandon teenagers in digital spaces nor to keep them away from them, as young people's mental health deserves better than a clash between technophiles and technophobes, writes child psychiatrist Pierre Fourneret in an op-ed for Le Monde.

items.title: In Russia-occupied Crimea, Ukrainian attacks land differently for divided residents
items.description: Crimea has been targeted this summer by a Ukrainian drone and missile offensive meant to isolate the Russian-occupied peninsula. While all sides are feeling the economic impact and loss of tourism, some are heartened and others resentful.

items.title: Nepal flooding deaths surpass 900 as needs climb
items.description: The confirmed death toll from Nepal’s catastrophic floods has surged to 903, with more than 4,200 still missing as rescue crews and humanitarian workers battle blocked highways to reach the hardest-hit areas, UN Spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said on Monday.

items.title: Niger's failed coup exposes cracks in the military — and Russia's influence
items.description: The failed coup in Niger has brought deep divisions within the military to light. As Russia's support highlights the junta's fading influence, soldiers continue to face jihadi attacks, poor equipment and little pay.

items.title: Ukraine's Drone War Exposes An Uncomfortable Reliance On China
